pp:ce:2007:q21.title: GATE CE 2007 | Set 1 | Question: 21
pp:ce:2007:q21.question:
For what values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ the following simultaneous equations have an infinite number of solutions ?
x + y + z = 5;
x + 3y + 3z = 9;
x + 2y + $\alpha$z = $\beta$

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra
detailed_solution.markdown:
The augmented matrix for this system is,

$$\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 &1 \\ 1& 3 & 3\\ 1 & 2 & \alpha \end{matrix}\right| \begin{matrix} 5\\ 9\\ \beta \end{matrix}\right ]$$

Using Gauss-elimination method we get

$$\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 &1 \\ 1& 3 & 3\\ 1 & 2 & \alpha \end{matrix}\right| \begin{matrix} 5\\ 9\\ \beta \end{matrix}\right ]\xrightarrow[R_{3}-R_{1}]{\overset{R_{2}-R_{1}}{\rightarrow}}\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 & 1\\ 0 & 2 & 2\\ 0 & 1 & \alpha -1 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 5\\ 4\\ \beta -5 \end{matrix} \right ]\xrightarrow[]{R_{3}-\frac{1}{2}R_{2}}\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 & 1\\ 0 & 2 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & \alpha -2 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 5\\ 4\\ \beta -7 \end{matrix} \right ]$$

Now, for infinite solution last row must be completely zero

i.e. $\alpha -2$ and $\beta -7=0$

$\Rightarrow \;\;\; \alpha =2$ and $\beta =7$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Ordinary Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{d\theta }{dt}&=-K\left ( \theta -\theta _{0} \right )\\ \text{(Newtons law }&\text{of cooling)} \\ \frac{d\theta }{\theta -\theta _{0}}&=-K\, dt \\ \int \frac{d\theta }{\theta -\theta _{0}}&=\int -Kdt \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \ln \left ( \theta -\theta _{0} \right )&=-Kt+C_{1} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \theta -\theta _{0}&=C.e^{-Kt} \\   \theta &=\theta _{0}+C.e^{-Kt}\\ \text{Given, } \theta _{0}&=25^{\circ}C \\ \text{Now at } t&=0,\, \theta =60^{\circ} \\  60&=25+ C.e^{0} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; C&=35 \\ \therefore \;\;  \theta &=25+35e^{-Kt} \\ \text{at } t&=15 \text{ minutes}\\ \theta &=40^{\circ}C \\ \therefore \; 40&=25+35e^{-K\times 15} \\ \Rightarrow \;e^{-15K}&=\frac{3}{7}\\ \text{Now at }t&=30 \text{ minutes}, \\ \theta &=25+35e^{-30K} \\  &=25+35\left ( e^{-15K} \right )^{2} \\  &=25+35\times \left ( \frac{3}{7} \right )^{2} \\    &=31.428^{\circ}C\approx 31.5^{\circ}C \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

detailed_solution.concept: Solid Mechanics - Deflection of Beams
detailed_solution.markdown:
Strain energy stored in a prismatic bar due to axial load $P_{1}$

$U_{1}=\frac{P_{1}^{2} L}{2 A E}$

Strain energy stored in a prismatic bar due to axial load, $P_{2}$

$U_{2}=\frac{P_{2}^{2} L}{2 A E}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

A plain sedimentation tank with a length of 20 m, width of 10 m, and a depth of 3 m is used in a water treatment plant to treat 4 million litres of water per day (4 MLD). The average temperature of water is 20$^{\circ}$C. The dynamic viscosity of water is $1.002 \times 10^{-3}N.s/m^2$ at 20$^{\circ}$C. Density of water is 998.2 $kg/m^3$. Average specific gravity of particles is 2.65.

What is the minimum diameter of the particle which can be removed with 100% efficiency in the above sedimentation tank ?

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Water Treatment
detailed_solution.markdown:
Settling velocity,

$$\begin{aligned} V_{s} &=\frac{H}{t} \\ \text{But} \; \; \; \; \; \; \; t&=\frac{Volume\; of\; tank}{Rate\; of\; flow} \\ &=\frac{20\times 10\times 3\times 24\times 60\times 60}{4\times 10^{6}\times 10^{-3}} \\ &=12960\; \text {seconds} \\ \therefore \; \; \; \; \; \; \; V_{s} &=\frac{3\times 1000}{12960}=0.2315\; \text{mm/s} \end{aligned}$$

Let the velocity of the particle which can be removed with 100% efficiency be ${V}'_{s}$ then

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{{V}'_{s}}{V_{s}}\times 100 &=100 \\ \Rightarrow {V}'_{s} &=V_{s} \\ \frac{g}{18}\left ( S_{s}-1 \right )\frac{d^{2}\rho }{\mu } &=0.2315\times 10^{-3} \\ \frac{9.81}{18}\left ( 2.65-1 \right )d^{2}\times \frac{998.2}{1.002\times 10^{-3}} &=0.2315\times 10^{-3} \\ d^{2}&=2.58\times 10^{-10} \\ d &=1.6\times 10^{-5}\text{m} \\ &=16\times 10^{-3}\text{mm} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.
